$comment: Generated by v2/tools/check-specs.mjs from ds-components/specs/*.spec.json. Do not edit. Every id here must have a test of the same name.

tests.text: The root is a button element, or with asChild a link. It is never a div or a span.
The type attribute is button unless the type prop says otherwise.
iconStart, iconEnd and the spinner carry aria-hidden.
Enter calls onClick once.
Space calls onClick once.
While disabled, a press does not call onClick.
While loading, a press does not call onClick.
While loading, the button keeps keyboard focus and stays in the Tab order, with aria-busy and aria-disabled set to true and the native disabled attribute absent.
With keyboard focus the root shows a ring at least 2 pixels thick with at least 3 to 1 contrast against what is beside it.
In every variant and state except disabled, the label has at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against the fill, in light and dark.
The root is at least 24 by 24 pixels at every size.
Where the pointer is coarse the root is at least 44 pixels tall.
A label too long for one line wraps inside the button and keeps its padding; it is never cut off.
Every DialogContent holds a DialogTitle with text. The generated test opens each example and fails when a DialogContent has no DialogTitle inside it; every example in this spec has one.
In development the adapter warns in the console when a DialogContent mounts without a DialogTitle or with an empty one, because Radix 1.3.1 does not warn.
While open, the content carries aria-modal set to true. Radix 1.3.1 does not set it; the adapter does.
aria-describedby on the content points at the description when one is given and is absent when none is.
The trigger has aria-haspopup set to dialog, aria-expanded that matches the open state, and while open aria-controls naming the content's id.
Enter and Space on the trigger open the dialog.
On open, focus moves inside the content: to the first control that is not a link, or to the content when there is none.
With content.initialFocus title, focus lands on the title and the top of the body stays in view.
Tab from the last control moves to the first, and focus never reaches the page behind.
Shift+Tab from the first control moves to the last.

With content.dismissible true, Escape closes the dialog and calls onOpenChange with false once. When a DropdownMenu inside the dialog is open, the first Escape closes only the menu and the dialog stays open.
With content.dismissible true, a primary-button press on the overlay closes the dialog. A right-click or Ctrl+click outside does not.
With content.dismissible false, neither Escape nor a press on the overlay closes the dialog or calls onOpenChange.
With content.dismissible false, the content holds at least one tabbable footer action that closes or completes the step, so a keyboard user is never trapped.
A press, Enter or Space on a close part closes the dialog.
With content.dismissible true, the footer holds at least one visible close part, such as Cancel, because a person using a touch screen reader has no Escape key and may not find the overlay.
On close, focus returns to the trigger.
A dialog opened by the open prop with no trigger returns focus on close to the element that had focus when it opened. Radix alone would leave focus on the page body.
While open, the page behind is hidden from assistive technology, cannot be pressed and does not scroll.
While open, the overlay covers the whole viewport and stays put when the page behind would scroll, and the content sits centred inside it.
At a 320 pixel wide viewport the content is the viewport width less the overlay's 16 pixel padding each side, centred, and the page has no horizontal scroll.
When the content is taller than the viewport less its margin, only the body scrolls; the header with the title and the footer with the actions stay fully visible.
Footer actions sit in one row aligned to the end while they fit, wrap onto further rows when they do not, and are never cut off or pushed outside the content.
A long title or description wraps, and a long word breaks rather than overflow; neither is cut off or ended with an ellipsis.
The title, description and body text have at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against the content's fill, in light and dark.
Where the person asks for reduced motion, the dialog and overlay appear and leave without a transition.
The trigger has aria-haspopup set to menu, aria-expanded set to true or false to match the menu, and aria-controls naming the content while it is open.
The content has role menu and aria-labelledby pointing at the trigger's id.

An item of any kind with a description has aria-labelledby pointing at its itemLabel and aria-describedby pointing at its itemDescription, so its accessible name is the label alone; type-ahead matches the label and never the description.
A group or radio group that has a label carries aria-labelledby pointing at that label's id. The adapter sets both ids, because Radix does not.
aria-checked on every checkbox and radio item matches its checked value, and exactly one radio item in a radio group with a value is checked.
The item indicator, iconStart, iconEnd and the shortcut hint carry aria-hidden.
An item with a shortcut hint carries the same shortcut in aria-keyshortcuts.
Enter on the closed trigger opens the menu with the first enabled item highlighted and focused.
Space on the closed trigger opens the menu with the first enabled item highlighted and focused.
ArrowDown on the closed trigger opens the menu with the first enabled item highlighted and focused.
ArrowDown moves the highlight to the next enabled item, skips disabled items, and stays on the last item while content.loop is false.
ArrowUp moves the highlight to the previous enabled item, skips disabled items, and stays on the first item while content.loop is false.
Home and PageUp move the highlight to the first enabled item.
End and PageDown move the highlight to the last enabled item.
Enter on a highlighted item calls its handler once, closes the menu and focuses the trigger.
Space on a highlighted item calls its handler once, closes the menu and focuses the trigger.
Escape closes the menu without calling any item's handler and focuses the trigger.
Tab inside the open menu leaves focus on the highlighted item and the menu open, as Radix does. A change to close on Tab, as the pattern describes, must change this test first.
Typing the first letters of an enabled item's label highlights it; disabled items are never matched.
After the menu closes by Escape or by choosing an item, focus is on the trigger.
Opened by pointer, focus is on the content and no item has data-highlighted until the mouse moves over one or an arrow key is pressed.
A disabled item has aria-disabled true, cannot be highlighted by arrow keys, type-ahead or the mouse, and pressing it calls no handler and leaves the menu open.
An item highlighted by the mouse and the same item highlighted by ArrowDown have the same computed background and text colour, and no item stylesheet rule uses :hover.
The highlighted item's background has at least 3 to 1 contrast against the content's background, in every variant, in light and dark.

The highlight never relies on colour alone: the highlighted item gains a filled block behind its whole width whose lightness differs from the content by at least 3 to 1, its text inverts against that fill, and with forced colours on an outline replaces the fill. A checked checkbox or radio item shows its check mark or dot, never only a colour.
Every label, description, group label and shortcut hint has at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against its background, highlighted or not, in every variant, in light and dark. Disabled items are exempt.
With forced colours on, the highlighted item shows an outline at least 2 pixels thick and the others show none.
Every item is at least 24 pixels tall and as wide as the content.
Where the pointer is coarse every item is at least 44 pixels tall.

Each item lays out in one row, in reading order: the indicator box or iconStart, then a column holding the label with the description under it, then iconEnd, then the shortcut hint at the end edge. The label column takes the remaining width, the icons and indicator box never shrink, and the shortcut does not wrap. The extensions stylesheet writes this.
A label or description too long for one line wraps inside the item, which grows taller and keeps its padding; it is never cut off or hidden behind the shortcut.

The separator is one line, 1 pixel (width/sm) thick, in border/primary/default, across the content's inner width, drawn on its block-start edge only, with space above and below it. The extensions stylesheet writes the one-sided border, the zero height and the space.

At 320 pixels wide the open content lies wholly inside the viewport, at least content.collisionPadding from each edge, and no page scrolls sideways. Because menu/max (320) is wider than the 304 pixels left inside the padding, the extensions stylesheet also caps the width at --radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-width.

Content taller than the space Radix reports as available is capped at that height and scrolls inside itself, so every item can be reached on a short phone screen. The extensions stylesheet sets the maximum height from --radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height and the vertical overflow.
While open with modal true, the rest of the page is hidden from assistive technology, does not scroll and ignores presses; a press outside closes the menu.
The input part is an input element. It is never a div with contenteditable.
Without an id prop the input gets a unique id from useId, and the label's for, the description's id and the error message's id are made from it. Two inputs on one page never share an id.
aria-describedby on the input lists the error message's id first while it is shown, then the description's id when there is one, and never an id that is not in the page.
aria-invalid is true on the input only while the error message is shown, and is absent otherwise.
An error is shown by words and an icon and a 2 pixel edge, never by colour alone.
A required field shows the word Required next to its label and sets the native required attribute. It is never marked by colour alone.
Tab reaches the input when it is enabled or read-only and skips it when disabled.
Enter in the input submits the enclosing form; the component does not cancel it.
While the input has focus the control shows a ring at least 2 pixels thick with at least 3 to 1 contrast against what is beside it, and the input shows no second outline of its own.
The control's edge has at least 3 to 1 contrast against the page in every state except disabled, in light and dark.
The placeholder has at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against the control's fill in light and dark. It fails in light today until the text/placeholder override lands.
Where the pointer is coarse the input's text is at least 16 pixels at every size, so iOS does not zoom the page on focus.
Where the pointer is coarse the control is at least 44 pixels tall.
The control is at least 24 by 24 pixels at every size.
At 320 pixels wide and at 200 percent text size, nothing in the field is clipped or hidden: the control grows taller, and the label, description and error message wrap.
With text at 200 percent the control is never shorter than its text; it uses a least height, not a fixed one.
The label, the control, the description and the error message stack top to bottom in that order, spaced by the root gap, and the error icon sits before the error words on their first line.

The prefix, the input and the suffix sit on one row inside the control, centred vertically. The input takes the width that is left and may shrink; the prefix and suffix keep their size. At 320 pixels wide the typed text never runs under the prefix or the suffix.
The prefix, the suffix, the required mark and the error icon carry aria-hidden.
A press on the control outside the input, including on the prefix or suffix, moves focus to the input.
The list has role tablist, each tab is a button element with role tab, and each panel has role tabpanel. A tab is never a link.
Exactly one tab has aria-selected true at all times. value or defaultValue is required by the type of the props, because Radix starts with no tab selected without one.
Each tab's aria-controls names its panel's id and each panel's aria-labelledby names its tab's id.
Panels of tabs that are not selected carry the hidden attribute and are not in the accessibility tree.
iconStart and iconEnd carry aria-hidden, so the tab's name comes from its label alone.
Tab from the element before the list moves focus onto the selected tab, not the first tab.
The shown panel has tabindex 0, so Tab from the selected tab reaches it.
Shift+Tab from any tab moves focus to the element before the list, not to another tab.
When horizontal, ArrowRight moves focus to the next tab that is not disabled, wrapping from last to first while list.loop is true, and ArrowUp and ArrowDown do nothing.
When horizontal, ArrowLeft moves focus to the previous tab that is not disabled, wrapping from first to last while list.loop is true.
When vertical, ArrowDown moves focus to the next tab that is not disabled, wrapping while list.loop is true, and ArrowLeft and ArrowRight do nothing.
When vertical, ArrowUp moves focus to the previous tab that is not disabled, wrapping while list.loop is true.
Home moves focus to the first tab that is not disabled.
End moves focus to the last tab that is not disabled.
PageUp moves focus to the first tab that is not disabled, as Radix provides.
PageDown moves focus to the last tab that is not disabled, as Radix provides.
In rtl, ArrowLeft moves to the next tab and ArrowRight to the previous one.
With activationMode manual, the arrow keys move focus without changing the selected tab, and Enter selects the focused tab.
With activationMode manual, Space selects the focused tab, as Enter does.
A disabled tab cannot be selected by press or by key, and the arrow keys skip it.

With keyboard focus a tab, or the shown panel, shows a ring 2 pixels thick, 2 pixels away, with at least 3 to 1 contrast against the page. The ring of the first and the last tab is fully visible and not cut off by the list's scrolling.
In both variants and both themes, every label that is not disabled has at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against what is behind it, including while hovered.
The mark of the selected tab, the brand line in line or the fill in pill, has at least 3 to 1 contrast against the page in light and dark.
The selected tab differs from the others by a shape, the line or the fill, and by a heavier label weight, not by colour alone.
In forced colours the selected tab is still marked: the line variant keeps its line and the pill variant shows a 2 pixel border.

When the tabs are wider than the list, the list scrolls sideways inside itself. At 320 pixels wide the page has no horizontal scroll. Labels never wrap and are never cut off with an ellipsis. The overflow and the single line are written in the extensions stylesheet.
A tab that receives focus from an arrow key is scrolled into view inside the list.
When the list scrolls, the selected tab is scrolled into view when Tabs first renders.

Horizontal tabs sit in a row above their panel; vertical tabs sit in a column at the inline start of their panel, each tab as wide as the list. The extensions stylesheet sets this from data-orientation, because the style declarations have no layout direction.

With list.behavior fill, the list is as wide as its container and every tab has the same width, within one pixel; with hug, each tab is as wide as its label and padding. When fill's labels do not fit, the list scrolls instead of cutting a label. The equal share is written in the extensions stylesheet.

The indicator draws a border width/md thick on one edge only: the bottom edge of the tab when horizontal and the inline-start edge when vertical, along the tab's full length. It is written in the extensions stylesheet; the style rules set only its colour.
Selecting a tab does not change its width or move the tabs beside it, although the label's weight changes: the extensions stylesheet reserves the width of the heavier weight.
Every tab is at least 24 by 24 pixels at every size.
Where the pointer is coarse every tab is at least 44 pixels tall.
